# costperrun

> A free calculator for what one multi-step AI agent run actually costs. It models the quadratic growth in billed input tokens caused by an agent re-sending its entire context on every step, across 17 models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Moonshot and DeepSeek.

Language models are stateless. An agent must re-send its whole history on every step, so total input tokens across N steps come out as:

    N × (system + user) + (output + tool_result) × N × (N−1) / 2

The second term is quadratic. Doubling the step count roughly quadruples the input cost. Most LLM pricing calculators price a single request, which is correct for a chatbot and understates agent cost by several times.

Worked example, a 12-step agent with a 2,000-token system prompt, a 500-token task, and 400 output plus 1,200 tool-result tokens per step:

- Raw conversation length: 21,700 tokens
- Billed input at a 0% retry rate: 135,600 tokens, a 6.2x multiplier
- Billed input at a 10% retry rate: 149,160 tokens, a 6.9x multiplier

The multiplier grows with step count: about 1.7x at 3 steps, 6.2x at 12, 10.3x at 20, 25.3x at 50 and 50.3x at 100.

The three levers that reduce it, in order of effect: prompt caching, because cache reads cost roughly 90% less and most of the bill is context re-sent verbatim; step count, because it is superlinear while price is linear; and tool-result size, because every tool result is re-sent by every later step.

## Pages

- [Calculator](https://costperrun.com/): The tool itself. Set steps, tool-result size, retry rate and cache hit rate, then compare 17 models, see cost attribution by component, and read the per-step accumulation table. Runs entirely in the browser.
- [Method and FAQ](https://costperrun.com/#method): Derivation of the formula, the worked example, the three levers ranked, and a plain statement of what the model does not cover.

## Data

- [models.json](https://costperrun.com/models.json): The canonical pricing dataset. Every rate carries the provider's own pricing URL and the date it was verified.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/pop3zxcv/costperrun): Full source. Stale prices can be reported as issues.

## Limitations

- Retries are modelled as a flat multiplier on total cost. Real retries occur at a specific context depth, so failures late in a run are under-counted.
- Cache hit rate is a single figure rather than per-prefix.
- Cache writes are not modelled. OpenAI's GPT-5.6 charges 1.25x uncached input to write to cache; only reads are priced.
- Batch API and long-context pricing tiers are not included.
- Providers use different tokenizers, so cross-vendor token counts are approximate.
- Tiered pricing is flattened, and the direction of the error differs by provider. DeepSeek bills peak and off-peak, with off-peak half of peak; the figures here are peak, so a run scheduled off-peak costs about half what is shown. OpenAI, xAI and Google raise rates once a single request crosses 200K tokens, and the figures here are the base tier, so a long agent is undercharged. Grok doubles every rate at that point; GPT-5.6 Sol goes from $4/$20 to $8/$30. On the default workload the largest single request is about 81K tokens at 50 steps, so this only bites past roughly 125 steps.
- Output is a planning estimate, not a billing forecast.

## Notes

- Prices verified 23 August 2026 against each provider's own pricing page.
- Claude Sonnet 5's $2/$10 rate is introductory and reverts to $3/$15 on 1 September 2026.
- Gemini 3.6 Flash and 3.7 Flash are on promotional rates of $0.75/$3.75 through 31 December 2026 and double on 1 January 2027.
- No tracking, no signup, no analytics. The Content-Security-Policy is `default-src 'none'`, so the page cannot make outbound requests.
